description: Ask 14 public DoH resolvers in North and South America, Europe and Asia (Google, Cloudflare, Quad9, CIRA, Comcast, Mullvad, DNSPod, IIJ, DNS.SB and more) for one record type at one name, and report whether they agree. Use it after changing a record to see whether the change has spread. `resolvers[]` gives every resolver's answer (`values`, `ttl`, `status` agree / disagree / unavailable), so compare those with the value you published; `records[]` is the most common answer and `analysis.propagation_pct` the share of answering resolvers that gave it (null, like `analysis.record_absent`, when verdict is incomplete). `verdict` is consistent (all agree), absent (all agree there is no record), rotating (a resolver changed its own answer when asked again: load balancing), split_short_ttl (answers differ and every TTL is 300 s or less: CDN or GeoDNS), split (answers differ with no such explanation: finding RESOLVERS_DISAGREE, status warn) or incomplete (fewer than half answered: finding RESOLVERS_PARTIAL, status warn). Otherwise status is info: this tool reports data, not a grade. A timeout is never counted as "no record"; if no resolver answers, the result is a retriable DOH_TIMEOUT error. Not cached, so you can poll it, but it has its own rate limit, lower than the other tools: poll no more often than every 10 seconds, and on error -32029 wait retry_after seconds. Each call queries all 14 resolvers (twice when they disagree). Read-only.

domain.description: Name to look up, e.g. "example.com", "_dmarc.example.com" or "_sip._tls.example.com". No scheme, no path.

type.description: Record type, upper case. Defaults to A.

name: check_dns_propagation

analysis.description: Tool-specific detail; its fields are typed in the resource mcp://tamingdns/resources/analysis/<tool name>.
